data.name: Justian
data.gender_notes: Justian is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'Justus', meaning 'just' or 'righteous'. In Christian tradition, the name Justian is often given in honor of St. Justin Martyr, an early Christian philosopher and apologist. He is known for his writings defending the Christian faith and is often invoked for issues of truth and justice. The name Justian carries the meaning “Just, Righteous” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Latin. Parents who choose Justian usually hope their child will grow to embody just, righteous and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes a commitment to living a just and righteous life in accordance with Christian teachings.
data.etymology: Justian belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Just, Righteous.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Justian total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_greek.name: Τζουστιάν
in_greek.meaning: Το Τζουστιάν σημαίνει δίκαιος και έντιμος
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Τζουστιάν προέρχεται από τη λατινική λέξη 'Iustus', που σημαίνει δίκαιος ή έντιμος. Είναι συνδεδεμένο με την έννοια της δικαιοσύνης και της ηθικής, αντανακλώντας ιδιότητες δικαιοσύνης και ηθικής καθαρότητας. Στην παλιά Εκκλησία, το όνομα αυτό ήταν δημοφιλές λόγω της σύνδεσής του με την αρετή.

historical_references.reference: Justinian I, also known as Flavius Petrus Sabbatius Justinianus, was a Roman Emperor from 527 to 565 AD, renowned for his reforms and initiatives in law and administration.

Justina of Nicomedia, also known as Justina the Great, was a Christian empress of the Eastern Roman Empire from 353 to 361 AD. She played a significant role in the religious policies of her time, especially regarding Arianism and the persecution of orthodox Christians.
